subject: FinTechCo — Pricing follow-up & US/EU residency impact
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@fintechco.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: FinTechCo — Pricing follow-up & US/EU residency impact

Hi Raj / Sofia,

Thanks again for the call this morning — useful conversation and appreciated the transparency on volumes and residency requirements. Quick recap and next steps below.

Recap / Signals:
- Projected starting volume: 10M–50M tokens/month (Q3).
- Growth path: target ~300M tokens/month within 12 months if initial integration performs to SLA.
- Residency requirement: EU data residency for EU traffic / EU customers (must store and process data in EU).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 300ms for standard generation paths (important for user experience).
- Budget: initial quoted monthly budget range $5k–$20k; long-term target ~$50–$60k/month as usage grows.

Pricing / qualification asks we discussed:
1) Effective unit economics target: you mentioned aiming for ~ $15 / 1M tokens (target for US-hosted workloads).
2) Want to understand delta for EU residency (hosting and processing wholly in EU).
3) Clarify whether we can count caching/batching reductions against billed tokens (and roughly how much benefit you expect).

What we’ll do next (action items):
- I’ll send a ballpark, tiered pricing summary (hosted vs. dedicated reserved) and call out EU premium. See attached high-level pricing sheet.
- If that looks reasonable, we’ll draft a mutual action plan / timeline and provide a formal quote and contract draft.
- You to share procurement timeline and any specific security artifacts needed (SOC2, AIA, DPAs).

Attached: redwood-pricing-sheet-20270428.pdf (summary), SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (security overview).

If useful, I can propose a quick follow-up next week to walk through specific numbers and a proposed canary plan for EU residency.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-pricing-sheet-20270428.pdf (pricing summary)

From: Raj Patel <raj@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia@fintechco.com>, Maya Chen <maya@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T14:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: FinTechCo — Pricing follow-up & US/EU residency impact

Thanks Dylan — short answers and a couple of clarifying Qs inline.

Quick confirmation: target ~$15 / 1M tokens (US) is what our product team would like to hit once we scale. Initial budget for Q3 is closer to $5k–$10k while we validate.

Questions:
1) At the volumes we mentioned (10M–50M/mo) can you give a couple of ballpark per-1M numbers for hosted vs. dedicated/reserved? Specifically want to understand the commit levels needed to get to $15 / 1M.
2) EU residency: does that require a separate EU-hosted cluster and therefore an additional per-token premium? If so, roughly how much?
3) Caching: we use a lot of repeated prefixes for customer onboarding flows — can you estimate how much we should assume for effective token reduction (billing) due to prefix/KV caching? Even a conservative 10–20% ballpark would help model TCO.

Procurement note: I’m attaching our procurement timeline and procurement lead (Maya) is looped here. We’ll need SOC2 evidence and a standard DPA. Please also include any typical lead times for Reserved capacity setup (if applicable).

Appreciate the quick follow-up — a short call next week to confirm would help.

Best,
Raj
Head of Product
FinTechCo

--
Attachment: fintechco-procurement-timeline.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@fintechco.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinTechCo — Pricing follow-up & US/EU residency impact

Raj — thanks, good clarifying questions. Below is a concise, actionable set of ballpark numbers and notes; I’ll follow up with a formal quote if these align with you.

Ballpark pricing (hosted, per-1M tokens) — baseline gen model:
- Hosted (US): $18 / 1M tokens (no commit).
- Hosted (EU residency): ~ +20% premium over US hosted => ~ $21.60 / 1M tokens (covers dedicated EU infra, data egress/ops).
- Dedicated / Reserved Capacity: starts around $12 / 1M tokens at commit levels in the 100M+ tokens/month range (12–24 month commit typical) — depends on GPU profile and concurrency.

Notes on effective billing and caching:
- Prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching typically reduce billed tokens by ~10–20% in practice; recommend modeling a conservative 15% reduction for budgeting.
- If you expect a high cache hit rate for onboarding flows, we can run a short eval to estimate savings more precisely.

Implications for your targets:
- To reach your target ~$15 / 1M in practice, you’d likely need a reserved-capacity agreement at mid-to-high commit (50–100M+ monthly) or a short promotional discount during initial scale-up.
- With EU residency and the ~20% premium, the effective target would be closer to $18–$19 / 1M unless we offset via a commit or promo.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll open a HubSpot deal (link below) and draft a mutual action plan aligned to your procurement timeline.
2) If you want, we can run a 2–4 week evaluation in the EU region (hosted) to model latency and caching savings; we’ll provide sample telemetry that you can verify.
3) I’ll work with Marissa on a reserved-capacity quote if you want committed pricing and with Sean on potential promotional discount.

Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet-20270428.pdf, SOC2-summary-2026.pdf

If these numbers look directionally correct, let me know and I’ll push the formal quote + MAP. Happy to set a 30-min follow-up next Tue or Wed.

Best,
Dylan
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Quoted pricing is illustrative; final quote will be provided in formal proposal.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: FinTechCo — EU residency pricing approval request (FIN-2027-0428)

Quick internal note — FinTechCo is interested in reaching ~$15 / 1M tokens target (US) once they scale; currently low starting budget but growth to ~300M/mo is plausible. They require EU residency for EU traffic.

I proposed: hosted US $18/1M, hosted EU +20% (~$21.6/1M), reserved starts ~ $12/1M at 100M+ commit. I noted caching could reduce billed tokens ~15%.

Requesting:
- Marissa: can we provisionally approve a 3-month promotional credit / ramp discount to help them validate in EU while they scale? Something like 20% off hosted EU pricing for first 90 days to get them to a committed POC.
- Sean: any concerns on SOC2/DPA turn times for this account? They shared procurement timeline (attached on thread).

If approved I’ll prepare the MAP and formal quote (deal id FIN-2027-0428) and propose an EU canary plan.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Attachment: redwood-pricing-sheet-20270428.pdf; SOC2-summary-2026.pdf
